all at walk_locals_pat's inner floor, byte-identical m3 output). The
wildcard rest ..._ was compiled as an EXACT-LENGTH pattern in BOTH
layers: each independently mapped the "_" rest to None to answer the
binding question, destroying the presence fact the predicate reads
(None → count==prefix, Some → count>=prefix). The wheel's own
walk_locals_pat matches [b0, ..._] on alternation branches — with
2+ branches the exact-1 predicate failed every arm and the exhaustive
floor fired. Both layers even rationalized it in comments.

emit_control's bind skips "_" (the wheel's bind_pat_rest law).
Wheel: parse_pat_list_args keeps Some(rest_name) unconditionally; the
four downstream _-skips (bind_pat_rest, both binder collectors,
pat_binders' rest) route through field_name_eq so the skip actually
fires through m2 (bare == on a parsed-vs-interned "_" was pointer-eq
false — the skips were dead code under m2, silently binding _ locals).

load; the canonical demo and its checksum TSV are regenerated.

The round boundary decided nothing and charged for it. The match has
always ended on MATCH_WIN_THRESHOLD kills -- MATCH_WIN_THRESHOLD's own
comment says the scoring rule is first-to-5-kills and that the round
timer "doesn't independently end the match" -- so every 30 seconds the
game spent 240 frames (4.0 s) crossing a boundary that changed nothing
on the scoreboard, and deleted CatchStreak on the way through. The
perfect-catch ladder is the game's signature skill expression. Wiping it
on a timer meant the clock's ONLY gameplay effect was punishing whoever
had built one.

Four changes, one bump, so they share one matrix run:

CatchStreak now survives a round boundary. Dying takes it (tick_respawn)
and a missed catch takes it. A timer does not.

Taunting breaks SpawnGuard. TAUNT_FRAMES (42) fits inside

the respawn tick completed entirely inside invulnerability -- a free
streak tier every death, with none of the vulnerability the move is
priced around, and flatly against SpawnGuard's own doc promise that it
"can never be an offensive shield". The tier is still earned; it is
simply no longer earned for free. With the streak surviving boundaries
the taunt is now a real risk/reward rather than a move whose payout the
clock deleted.

two-top/fb8c886:
Two theater bugs, one message because they share a screen.

The scrub loop. Dragging the timeline sent the playhead into an
oscillation it never left. Three causes compounded. A seek fast-forwards
Time<Virtual> at 64x and bevy_ggrs bursts a chunk of ticks in one frame,
so it lands past the target. The drag then re-issued the seek every frame
from the held finger, and once the playhead sat past the target the
still-held finger re-targeted backward, overshot again, forever. Each
backward seek also ran retain(|s| s.frame < target) over the snapshot
ring, gutting it a little more each pass until nearest_before returned
nothing and seeking died outright.

The sim reads ggrs-provided PlayerInputs, so it can't be single-stepped
outside the driver; the fix is at the input and snapshot layer. A held
finger now issues exactly one seek (scrub_debounce), so a landed or
overshot playhead is never re-targeted. The snapshot ring is a monotonic
read cache and is never pruned on a seek; a frame's snapshot is
deterministic and a later forward seek reuses it. A snapshot banks on
frame 1 as well as every second, so a backward seek can always reach the
start of the tape. Capture is idempotent by frame so replayed frames
don't duplicate.

The exit. Every menu puts a bordered BACK button at the tap target; the
theater had a thin line of text at the top, easy to miss when the bottom
(where a menu's BACK lives) is the scrub strip. You tap the bottom, it
scrubs, and you conclude there's no way out. The theater now shows the
same bordered BACK button, at the top because the bottom is scrub, which
matches the live match's top exit. The whole top band still taps to
leave; the box just says where.

Ordered theater_input -> capture -> drive so a seek issued this frame is
consumed this frame. Pure helpers (scrub_debounce, should_snapshot) are
unit-tested; a held finger seeks once and snapshots cover the whole tape.
No sim change; SIM_VERSION untouched.
clob/fb697a8:
Computational mechanics defines the causal states of a process as
equivalence classes of histories with identical conditional future
distributions -- two pasts belong together exactly when they predict
the same future. The minimal maximally-predictive model (the
epsilon-machine) is built from those classes, so they are what a
crystallization loop should converge toward. Hidden-state k-means only
approximates that when the core's geometry already separates
predictive circumstances; a frozen or half-trained core mixes them,
and the distill coherence gate then rejects the blend wholesale --
episodes with perfectly learnable futures get discarded because they
were binned by geometry instead of by consequence.

This makes futures the organizing principle instead of the veto:

- Episode gains a  field: the observed continuation starting
  at actual_token, recorded to a horizon of 8 by both ingest paths.
  Old ring files deserialize as None and are skipped; the ring is
  per-run scratch, not an artifact.
- src/crystal/causal.rs refines the k-means partition: SPLIT clusters
  along future fault lines (subgroups with identical future prefixes
  that can stand alone become their own clusters), then MERGE clusters
  whose next-token distributions sit within a Jensen-Shannon threshold.
  Merging on futures alone is the causal-state definition; the MDL
  gate downstream still vetoes any merge too scattered to compress.
  Deterministic: same episodes in, same partition out.
- CrystalConfig.causal opts the engine cycle in;  exposes it.

Verified end to end on the planted-pattern diagnostic corpus with the
frozen random small core (seed 42, 6000 tokens, 318 episodes):

  state-only:  8 clusters -> 0 modules (as in every prior run)
  causal:      8 -> 20 clusters -> 4 modules, 67 episodes consumed
  eval A/B, equal compute, 1945 predictions:
    modules cleared  mean NLL 7.0494
    modules loaded   mean NLL 7.0304  (-0.27%)

The pie pump rewrote every playing clip's --pct each frame — a conic-
gradient repaint per clip per frame on the A16's GPU for moves far under
half a percent. Writes now quantize to 0.5% (pies) and quarter-pixels
(playhead) and skip when unchanged; a pie on a 2-bar loop repaints every
frame or two instead of sixty times a second, still reading the audio
clock on every write that lands.

The ? page gains a persisted sync nudge (±250 ms, 10 ms steps) applied
inside visualLatency, so pies, playhead, and editor cursors shift as one.
This is the correction for platforms whose outputLatency estimate lies —
Android reports 0 on some builds and goes stale over Bluetooth, which
reads as visuals leading or trailing the sound no matter how exact the
clock math is. Smoke covers persistence.
